# FEPAR — Festac Pan African Renaissance

FEPAR is a Pan-African platform connecting enterprise, diaspora partnerships, creative industries, youth talent, development, infrastructure, cultural rights, heritage, research and community-led action across Africa and its global diaspora. In the lead-up to the 2027 50th anniversary of FESTAC '77, the site presents a FEPAR invitation to remember, reconnect and imagine a digital “Second Homecoming.”

## Main routes
- [FEPAR](https://www.fepar.africa/): Anniversary-led platform overview and a FEPAR invitation to remember, reconnect and imagine a digital “Second Homecoming.”
- [FESTAC '77 at 50](https://www.fepar.africa/festac-50/): Sourced 1966–1977–2027 timeline and invitation-stage vision; proposed archive, directory, grant and event features are not live services.
- [FESTAC History](https://www.fepar.africa/festac-history/): A sourced introduction to the Benin Kingdom, Queen Mother Idia, the FESTAC ’77 emblem and related cultural memory.
- [FEPAR Theme Songs](https://www.fepar.africa/theme-songs/): Listening room for FEPAR theme songs and licensed music collaborations; tracks appear when approved audio is published.
- [What We Do](https://www.fepar.africa/what-we-do/): Detailed focus areas, possible collaboration pathways, potential partners and ways to begin a conversation.
- [Fepar Diaspora Limited](https://www.fepar.africa/diaspora/): Diaspora relationships, development thinking and infrastructure-minded partnerships.
- [Fepar Records Ltd](https://www.fepar.africa/records/): Artist and producer pathways, music, cultural rights and collaboration.
- [Development & Impact](https://www.fepar.africa/development/): Partnership priorities for youth, talent, cultural rights, infrastructure, diaspora connection and research.
- [Contact](https://www.fepar.africa/contact/): Partnership, development, records and general inquiries.

FEPAR focus areas describe priorities and possible partnership pathways, not claims that every programme or service is active. Development topics are not claims of completed projects.
